```md codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/REVIEW-dind-dev.md
# Review — codx-junior DEV in the DIND image

Reviewed: the DIND deployment compose against
`codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/` (Dockerfile, `entrypoint-wrapper.sh`,
`codx-junior-dind-init.sh`, `docker-compose.example.yaml`) and the inner stack
`codx-junior-installer/codx-junior/docker-compose.yaml`.

**Verdict:** the architecture of the compose is right (nested dockerd, source
mounted, outer Traefik → container:80 → inner Traefik), but as written the stack
does not come up in dev mode. Six blocking defects, listed below with the fix
that is now in the tree. The corrected compose is
`docker-compose.dev.example.yaml`.

## Image published (rebuild + publish done)

`codxjuniorai/codx-junior:dind` was rebuilt from this tree and pushed:

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Tag | `codxjuniorai/codx-junior:dind` |
| Immutable tag | `codxjuniorai/codx-junior:dind-2026-11-20` |
| Digest | `sha256:b2b66129aa489d0d2a935e484751648ce307583c0574a48272edbe4d7641c0a3` |
| Platform | `linux/amd64` |
| Baked scripts | `entrypoint-wrapper.sh`, `codx-junior-dind-init.sh`, `coolify-install.sh` **with the fixes above** |

The old `codxjunior/codx-junior:dind` tag (2026-01-29) is **not** updated and
cannot be: the registry token has no write access to the `codxjunior` org
(`denied: requested access to the resource is denied`). Both compose examples now
point at `codxjuniorai/codx-junior:dind`; pullers of the old path must switch.

### Why the previous build attempts failed — root cause

The dind image was built with the **repository root** as context
(`-f .../codx-junior-dind/Dockerfile .`), and the root `.dockerignore` contains

```
codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/
```

so the three scripts the Dockerfile COPYs were stripped from the context, while
the remaining ~1 GB of sources made this host's buildkit die with a
`contenthash` panic during context hashing. The image is now **self-contained**:
context = `codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind` (own `.dockerignore`, ~4 files),
Dockerfile COPYs `./<script>`, and `build.sh` builds from that folder. Build time
dropped to seconds and the crash is gone.

## Local compose — the final version to run on a machine that already has Traefik

`docker-compose.local.yaml` is the runnable version of the composed stack for a
local host that already runs Traefik and already resolves the domain. Nothing in
it is host-specific: every path, domain, network and entrypoint name is a
variable with a working default, so it starts without any extra file.

What changed against the compose that was posted:

| Posted compose | `docker-compose.local.yaml` |
|---|---|
| `/home/shared/...` absolute paths | `${CODX_JUNIOR_CHECKOUT:-../..}` = the checkout you run from; projects in a named volume, or `CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS` |
| `env_file: ./.env` | none — the outer container needs no `.env`; the inner stack bootstraps its own from `.env.example` |
| network `docker_default` (external) | one external network named by `TRAEFIK_NETWORK` (default `traefik`) plus the `traefik.docker.network` label |
| domain, entrypoints, certresolver hard-coded | `CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN`, `TRAEFIK_WEB_ENTRYPOINT`, `TRAEFIK_WEBSECURE_ENTRYPOINT`, `TRAEFIK_CERT_RESOLVER`, `ROUTER_NAME` |
| `runtime: sysbox-runc` / `privileged` unclear | `privileged: true` by default, sysbox documented as the alternative |
| `/dev/ppp` mounted unconditionally | commented out (enable it on a Linux host that has it, otherwise the default workspace is skipped) |
| — | no host port is published, by design: your Traefik dials container **80** (the inner Traefik); your host 80/443 are left alone |

Variables (all optional, defaults in brackets):

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN` [`codx-junior.localhost`] | The single host served; used by the outer router **and** by every inner Traefik rule |
| `TRAEFIK_NETWORK` [`traefik`] | Docker network of your Traefik (`docker network ls`) |
| `TRAEFIK_WEB_ENTRYPOINT` / `TRAEFIK_WEBSECURE_ENTRYPOINT` [`web` / `websecure`] | Your Traefik entrypoint names |
| `TRAEFIK_CERT_RESOLVER` [`letsencrypt`] | Your ACME resolver name |
| `ROUTER_NAME` [`codx-junior-local`] | Router/middleware/service names — change it to run two stacks side by side |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_CHECKOUT` [`../..`] | Repository root on the host |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS` [named volume] | Host folder your projects live in (e.g. `$HOME/codx-junior-projects`) |
| `DEBUG` [`1`] | 1 = Vite dev server + debug API, 0 = the prebuilt client of the image |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_HIDDEN` [`0`] | 1 hides the platform's own checkout from the project picker (on a local test it is the only project, so it stays visible) |
| `GITHUB_ADMINS` [empty] | GitHub login(s) with admin rights — set yours |
| `USER_ID` / `GROUP_ID` [`1001`] | Passed to the inner stack and to the default workspace |

Run it (from the repository root; a `.env` next to the compose file works too):

```bash
export CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN=codx-junior.example.com
export GITHUB_ADMINS=<your-github-login>
export TRAEFIK_NETWORK=$(docker network ls --format '{{.Name}}' | grep -i traefik | head -1)

docker compose -f codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/docker-compose.local.yaml up -d
docker compose -f codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/docker-compose.local.yaml logs -f
```

The first boot takes ~10-15 minutes (the nested daemon pulls milvus/api/client
and builds `codx-junior-localai`), which is why the healthcheck `start_period` is
15 minutes. Then open `https://$CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN`.

If your Traefik has no ACME certificate for that host (a `.localhost` name, for
instance) it falls back to its default self-signed certificate — expected on a
local test, the browser only warns.

## How the image actually boots

1. `entrypoint-wrapper.sh` (ENTRYPOINT) starts the nested `dockerd`.
2. It sources every `/custom-cont-init.d/*.sh` in the same shell.
3. `codx-junior-dind-init.sh` `cd`s to
   `/home/codx-junior/codx-junior/codx-junior-installer/codx-junior` and runs
   `compose up -d`, then starts `workspaces/codx-junior-workspace-default`.
4. The wrapper keeps the container alive by following the stack logs.

The inner stack contains **its own Traefik** publishing `80`/`443` inside the
container, plus `codx-junior-api`, `codx-junior-client`, `milvus`, `localai`,
`codx-junior-analytics-init`, `codx-junior-init`. Therefore the outer Traefik must
target **container port 80** and nothing else. The inner api/client bind-mount
`../../.` (the checkout) over `/home/codx-junior/codx-junior`, which is what turns
this into a DEV deployment: the checkout must be mounted, otherwise the stacked
`up` has no compose file.

## Blocking findings

| # | Finding | Impact | Fix |
|---|---------|--------|-----|
| 1 | Inner scripts call `docker-compose` (compose **v1**). | On an image that only ships the v2 plugin the binary is absent; the call was backgrounded, so it failed silently and the stack never started. | `compose()` helper: `docker compose` when available, `docker-compose` as fallback (`entrypoint-wrapper.sh`, `codx-junior-dind-init.sh`). |
| 2 | Inner compose declares `env_file: .env` for localai/api/api-background/client, and a fresh checkout only has `.env.example`. | `compose up` aborts with `env file ... not found`: nothing starts. | Init script bootstraps `.env` from `.env.example` when missing. |
| 3 | `codx-junior-client` hard-codes `DEBUG=0`. | The `DEBUG=1` of the DIND container never reaches the client: no Vite dev server, the "dev mode" of the request does not happen. | `DEBUG=${DEBUG:-0}` in the inner compose (default still `0`, production untouched). |
| 4 | `Host('ai-first-it.codx-junior.ai')` — **single quotes**. | Traefik rule syntax requires backticks; the router is rejected as unparsable and the site 404s. That host is also absent from `CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN`, and the inner routers only match `Host(${CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN})`, so even a valid rule would hit the inner Traefik's default 404. | One host per deployment, backticks everywhere; the extra host was dropped. |
| 5 | `acme.json` mounted at `/codx-junior/traefik/letsencrypt/acme.json`. | Dead path: nothing reads it. The inner Traefik reads `/config/letsencrypt/acme.json` (`<checkout>/codx-junior-installer/codx-junior/traefik/letsencrypt/acme.json`), and TLS is terminated by the outer Traefik anyway. Worse, the file must already exist on the host or Docker creates a **directory** in its place. | Mount removed; the correct path is documented as optional. |
| 6 | `/dev/ppp` not mounted, while the default workspace stack (started by the init script) declares `devices: /dev/ppp`. | That inner `up` fails; the workspace is missing and the error is buried in the nested daemon logs. | `/dev/ppp:/dev/ppp` added (or stop starting that workspace). |

## Correctness / robustness findings (fixed)

- **Race in the init script.** `compose up -d &` was backgrounded and the
  workspace stack started immediately after, but that stack joins the external
  network `codx-junior_default` that the first `up` creates → intermittent
  `network ... not found`. `up -d` is now synchronous.
- **Restart loop in the wrapper.** It ended with
  `docker-compose logs --tail=0 --follow`: with the stack not yet created the
  command fails, and when a container is recreated the stream ends and the
  command returns — either way PID 1 exits and `restart: unless-stopped`
  reboots the whole nested Docker. It now re-attaches in a loop and falls back to
  `/var/log/dockerd.log` when the stack is absent.
- **`set -e` + sourced scripts.** The init scripts run inside the wrapper's
  shell: an `exit` there kills PID 1. They now `return` and log instead of dying,
  so a failed inner stack is inspectable.
- `rm /var/run/docker/containerd/containerd.pid` without `-f` would abort under
  `set -e` on a fresh container → `rm -f`.
- `working_dir: /codx-junior` removed: that path does not exist in the image
  (`COPY . /codx-junior` is commented out in the Dockerfile) and the wrapper does
  its own `cd`.
- `GITHUB_ADMINS="codx-junior"` in `docker-compose.example.yaml` passed the
  **literal quotes** as the value (plain YAML scalar) → the admin allowlist never
  matched. Fixed in the example.
- Router split: `websecure` router for the site, separate `web` router for the
  redirect, and a per-site middleware name so a shared host cannot collide.

## Things to know before deploying

- **`privileged: true` vs `runtime: sysbox-runc`** — the official example uses
  sysbox with `privileged: false`. They are alternatives, not a pair: `privileged`
  works on any host, sysbox is the safer one when the host has it. Keep exactly
  one.
- **Published tag is `amd64` only** (`codxjunior/codx-junior:dind`, last push
  2026-01-29). ARM hosts get `no matching manifest`. The tag is also older than
  the scripts in this folder: only `entrypoint-wrapper.sh` is replaceable by a
  bind mount, the baked `/custom-cont-init.d/codx-junior-dind-init.sh` is not. The
  dev compose mounts both so the fixes above apply without a rebuild; for a real
  rollout rebuild and republish the image.
- **First boot is long and heavy**: inside the nested daemon it pulls milvus,
  `codxjunior/codx-junior:debian|api|client` and builds `codx-junior-localai` from
  `./localai`. All of it lives in the `dind-storage` volume. Allow several GB and
  a long `start_period` (the healthcheck here waits 15 min).
- **`DEBUG=1` on the client needs `client/node_modules`.** `scripts/run_client.sh`
  runs `npm install` when `node_modules` is missing: the first dev start is slow
  and needs egress.
- **`/home/shared` mounted whole.** The inner api mounts the nested
  `/var/run/docker.sock` and every workspace container gets the same bind: the
  cloud's `acme.json` and other tenants' checkouts become reachable from the app.
  Mount only the projects you need on a shared host.
- The checkout is reachable twice (`/home/codx-junior/codx-junior` and under
  `/home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior/...`); set `CODX_JUNIOR_HIDDEN=1` to hide
  the platform project from the picker.
- The inner Traefik also publishes `443`, which the outer LB never uses (TLS ends
  at the outer Traefik). Harmless, just not needed.

## Verification

```bash
# 1. Bring it up
docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.example.yaml up -d

# 2. Nested daemon is alive
docker exec gbrian-codx-junior docker info --format '{{.ServerVersion}}'

# 3. Inner stack (this is the step that used to fail silently)
docker exec gbrian-codx-junior sh -c '
  cd /home/codx-junior/codx-junior/codx-junior-installer/codx-junior && \
  docker compose ps'
# expected: traefik-codx-junior, codx-junior-api, codx-junior-client,
#           codx-junior-api-background, milvus-codx-junior, localai-codx-junior

# 4. Dev mode really is dev mode (Vite dev server, not the prebuilt preview)
docker exec gbrian-codx-junior docker logs codx-junior-client 2>&1 | grep -E 'DEBUG|VITE|dev'

# 5. The outer router found the container on :80
curl -sI https://gbrian.codxjunior.com | head -1
```

1. Your comment: you posted the *original* compose (absolute `/home/shared/...` paths, `env_file: ./.env`, external network `docker_default`, rule with two hostnames) and asked for **the env file for that setup, written out here**.
2. Generating it exposed two holes in the compose I delivered: the second hostname (`ai-first-it.codx-junior.ai`) had nowhere to go, and the healthcheck probed `127.0.0.1/` without a `Host` header — the inner Traefik answers `404` to an unmatched Host, so the container could never be healthy.

## What I did

- **New `codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/.env.local.example`** — the env file for your host: checkout `/home/shared/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform`, projects `/home/shared`, domain `gbrian.codxjunior.com`, network `docker_default`, router `gbrian-junior-demo`, resolver `myresolver`, image `codxjunior/codx-junior:dind`, `CONTAINER_NAME=gbrian-codx-junior`, `DEBUG=1`. Every key the compose interpolates is there, with the value taken from your original request. Git ignores `**/.env` but not `.env.local.example`, so the template is committable.
- **`CODX_JUNIOR_EXTRA_HOSTS` added** to `docker-compose.local.yaml`: both routers append it to the rule, so your `|| Host('ai-first-it.codx-junior.ai')` is preserved. A `${ROUTER_NAME}-host` middleware rewrites `Host` to `CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN` — the inner Traefik only knows one host, so without it the alias matches outside and 404s inside.
- **Healthcheck fixed**: `CMD-SHELL` + `-H "Host: $$CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN"` (`$$` = no compose interpolation, the container shell expands it).
- **Not carried over** from your compose, on purpose: `working_dir: /codx-junior` (path does not exist in the image), `env_file: ./.env` (the inner stack builds its own `.env`), the `acme.json` mount (TLS ends at *your* Traefik; the inner one writes `codx-junior-installer/codx-junior/traefik/letsencrypt/acme.json` inside the checkout that is already mounted).
- **`REVIEW-dind-dev.md`** gained *"The `.env` of the host that already runs Traefik"* with the copy/pass commands and the three caveats above.
- **Validated**: `docker-compose -f .../docker-compose.local.yaml build definitely-not-a-service` → only `no such service: definitely-not-a-service` (parse + interpolation of the edited file clean, no unset-variable warnings). CISO change review on the folder: **allow**, 0 findings.

#########################################################################
##
## .env for docker-compose.local.yaml — tuned for the host that posted
## the original compose:
##
##   checkout   /home/shared/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform
##   projects   /home/shared
##   domain     gbrian.codxjunior.com  (+ ai-first-it.codx-junior.ai)
##   Traefik    already running on the host: external network `docker_default`,
##              resolver `myresolver`, routers named `gbrian-junior-demo*`
##
## How to use it. Compose v2 loads a `.env` placed in the folder of the
## compose file automatically:
##
##   cp codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/.env.local.example \
##      codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/.env
##   docker compose -f codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/docker-compose.local.yaml up -d
##
## If your compose CLI does not pick that up, pass the file explicitly (this
## always works, whatever the version):
##
##   docker compose \
##     --env-file codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/.env.local.example \
##     -f codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/docker-compose.local.yaml up -d
##
## Every key below is one the compose file interpolates. Deleting a line only
## brings back the default written inside the compose file.
##
## NO SECRET BELONGS HERE. The inner stack builds its own
## codx-junior-installer/codx-junior/.env from .env.example on first boot; the
## LiteLLM keys live there (edit it, never commit it — git ignores `**/.env`).
##
#########################################################################

# --- image and container name -----------------------------------------
# The compose that was posted used the codxjunior namespace; build.sh today
# publishes codxjuniorai/codx-junior:dind. Keep the one your host can pull.
CODX_JUNIOR_IMAGE=codxjunior/codx-junior:dind
CONTAINER_NAME=gbrian-codx-junior

# --- bind mounts ------------------------------------------------------
# Absolute on purpose: the checkout is NOT under the folder of the compose
# file, so the `../..` default would mount the wrong tree.
CODX_JUNIOR_CHECKOUT=/home/shared/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform
# What the app sees as /home/codx-junior-projects. /home/shared also contains
# the checkout, so the platform itself appears in the project picker.
CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS=/home/shared

# --- domain and the Traefik that already runs on this host -------------
# A host your Traefik already serves with a valid certificate.
CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN=gbrian.codxjunior.com
# Extra hostnames appended to the outer router rule. The outer Traefik also
# rewrites the Host header to CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN, because the inner Traefik
# only knows the primary domain. Leave it empty for a single hostname.
CODX_JUNIOR_EXTRA_HOSTS=" || Host('ai-first-it.codx-junior.ai')"
# External network created by that Traefik (`docker network ls`).
TRAEFIK_NETWORK=docker_default
# Names this site's routers/services/middlewares. Must stay unique on the host.
ROUTER_NAME=gbrian-junior-demo
# Entrypoint and certificate-resolver names OF YOUR TRAEFIK (not this stack).
TRAEFIK_WEB_ENTRYPOINT=web
TRAEFIK_WEBSECURE_ENTRYPOINT=websecure
TRAEFIK_CERT_RESOLVER=myresolver

# --- runtime ----------------------------------------------------------
# 1 = Vite dev server in codx-junior-client + debug API. The first start runs
# npm install, so it needs egress and time. 0 = prebuilt client from the image.
DEBUG=1
# GitHub logins allowed to administer the instance, comma separated.
# Replace with your own login.
GITHUB_ADMINS=gbrian
# 1 hides the platform's own checkout from the project picker.
# Kept at 0: on a first local run it is the only project available.
CODX_JUNIOR_HIDDEN=0
# Owner of the folders under CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS (id -u / id -g on the host).
USER_ID=911

#########################################################################
##
## .env for docker-compose.local.yaml — the host that posted the compose
##
##   checkout    /home/shared/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform
##   projects    /home/shared
##   domain      gbrian.codxjunior.com  (+ ai-first-it.codx-junior.ai)
##   Traefik     external network `docker_default`, resolver `myresolver`,
##               routers `gbrian-junior-demo*`, TLS terminated by that Traefik
##
## Compose loads the file automatically when it is named `.env` in the SAME
## folder as the compose file:
##
##   cp codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/.env.local.example \
##      codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/.env
##   docker compose -f codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/docker-compose.local.yaml up -d
##
## or keep this name and pass it explicitly:
##
##   docker compose --env-file codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/.env.local.example \
##     -f codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/docker-compose.local.yaml up -d
##
## Every key below is one the compose file interpolates; deleting one only
## brings back the default written in the compose file.
##
## NO SECRET LIVES HERE. The checkout's inner stack builds its own
## codx-junior-installer/codx-junior/.env from .env.example on first boot; the
## LiteLLM keys belong there (edit it, never commit it — .gitignore ignores it).
##
#########################################################################

# --- image and container name -----------------------------------------
# The namespace published by build.sh today is codxjuniorai; the compose that
# was posted used codxjunior. Keep the one your host can pull.
CODX_JUNIOR_IMAGE=codxjunior/codx-junior:dind
CONTAINER_NAME=gbrian-codx-junior

# --- bind mounts ------------------------------------------------------
# The checkout (repository root). Absolute on purpose: it is outside the
# folder of the compose file, so `../..` would point at the wrong tree.
CODX_JUNIOR_CHECKOUT=/home/shared/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform
# What the app sees as /home/codx-junior-projects. /home/shared already
# contains the checkout, so the platform also shows up in the picker.
CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS=/home/shared

# --- domain and the Traefik that already runs on this host -------------
# Must be a host that Traefik already serves with a valid certificate.
CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN=gbrian.codxjunior.com
# Extra hostnames appended to the outer router rule. The outer Traefik
# rewrites the Host header to CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN, because the inner
# Traefik only knows the primary domain. Leave empty for a single host.
CODX_JUNIOR_EXTRA_HOSTS=" || Host('ai-first-it.codx-junior.ai')"
# External network created by that Traefik (docker network ls).
TRAEFIK_NETWORK=docker_default
# Names the routers/services/middlewares of this site; keep it unique on the
# host. It must not be shared with another container.
ROUTER_NAME=gbrian-junior-demo
# Entrypoint and resolver names OF YOUR TRAEFIK.
TRAEFIK_WEB_ENTRYPOINT=web
TRAEFIK_WEBSECURE_ENTRYPOINT=websecure
TRAEFIK_CERT_RESOLVER=myresolver

# --- runtime ----------------------------------------------------------
# 1 = Vite dev server in codx-junior-client + debug API (slow first start:
# npm install needs egress). 0 = prebuilt client from the image.
DEBUG=1
# GitHub logins allowed to administer the instance, comma separated.
GITHUB_ADMINS=gbrian
# 1 hides the platform's own checkout from the project picker.
CODX_JUNIOR_HIDDEN=0
# Owner of the folders under CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS (id -u / id -g on the host).
USER_ID=911
GROUP_ID=911
# Only used by the inner Traefik's own ACME resolver, which your Traefik makes
# unnecessary; harmless if it never issues anything.
ACME_EMAIL=mail@mail.com
TZ=UTC

#########################################################################
##
## codx-junior — LOCAL run of the DIND image behind YOUR OWN Traefik
##
## Final, runnable version of the compose posted for review. Differences with
## docker-compose.dev.example.yaml: every host-specific path, domain, network
## and entrypoint name is a variable with a local-friendly default, there is no
## `env_file` (nothing outside the image needs one), and the outer Traefik is
## reached through a single parameterised external network.
##
## How it works
## ------------
## The container runs a *nested* Docker daemon. entrypoint-wrapper.sh starts
## dockerd, sources /custom-cont-init.d/*.sh and codx-junior-dind-init.sh brings
## up the inner stack (codx-junior-installer/codx-junior) plus the default
## workspace. The inner stack runs its OWN Traefik that binds :80/:443 *inside
## this container*, so your host Traefik only has to point at container port 80.
## No host port is published here: your existing 80/443 are left alone.
##
## Quick start (from the repository root)
## --------------------------------------
##   export CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN=codx-junior.localhost   # a host your Traefik serves
##   export GITHUB_ADMINS=<your-github-login>
##   export TRAEFIK_NETWORK=<your traefik network>     # docker network ls
##   docker compose -f codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/docker-compose.local.yaml up -d
##
## Every variable can also live in a `.env` file next to this file (compose
## reads it automatically). Defaults are chosen so the stack starts without one.
##
#########################################################################

# Fixed project name: volumes keep the same name whatever folder you run from.
name: codx-junior-local

services:
  codx-junior:
    image: ${CODX_JUNIOR_IMAGE:-codxjuniorai/codx-junior:dind}
    container_name: ${CONTAINER_NAME:-codx-junior-local}

    # A nested dockerd needs real privileges. Pick ONE of the two:
    #   privileged: true                        <- default, works on Linux and Docker Desktop
    #   runtime: sysbox-runc + privileged: false <- safer, only when the host has sysbox
    privileged: true
    restart: unless-stopped
    # The inner stack must be allowed to stop its own containers on shutdown.
    stop_grace_period: 30s

    # The first boot pulls milvus/debian/api/client and builds
    # codx-junior-localai *inside* the nested daemon; keep it from flapping
    # while that happens.
    healthcheck:
      # The inner Traefik answers 404 to an unmatched Host, so the probe sends
      # the real domain: `$$` stops compose from interpolating and the container
      # shell expands CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN at probe time.
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -fsS -o /dev/null -H \"Host: $$CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN\" http://127.0.0.1/"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 900s

    volumes:
      # REQUIRED — the checkout. The inner stack bind-mounts `../../.` over
      # /home/codx-junior/codx-junior in api/api-background/client; without it
      # the init script finds no compose file and starts nothing.
      # `../..` = the repository root, relative to THIS file.
      - ${CODX_JUNIOR_CHECKOUT:-../..}:/home/codx-junior/codx-junior

      # Projects folder seen by the inner api and by the workspace containers.
      # Default: a named volume, so a first run does not drop root-owned folders
      # inside the checkout. Point it at a real folder of yours to work on your
      # own code:  CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS=$HOME/codx-junior-projects
      - ${CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS:-codx-junior-projects}:/home/codx-junior-projects

      # DEV: run the checkout copies of the boot scripts instead of the baked
      # ones, so they can be edited without rebuilding the image. A file bind
      # mount follows the inode: editing in place works, `git checkout`/`mv`
      # over the file does not (restart the container after replacing it).
      - ${CODX_JUNIOR_CHECKOUT:-../..}/codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/entrypoint-wrapper.sh:/usr/local/bin/entrypoint-wrapper.sh:ro
      - ${CODX_JUNIOR_CHECKOUT:-../..}/codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/codx-junior-dind-init.sh:/custom-cont-init.d/codx-junior-dind-init.sh:ro

      - dind-certs-ca:/certs/ca
      - dind-certs-client:/certs/client

      # The default workspace stack declares `devices: /dev/ppp`; enable this on
      # a Linux host that has /dev/ppp. Without it that inner `up` fails and the
      # default workspace is simply missing (codx-junior-dind-init.sh only warns).
      # - /dev/ppp:/dev/ppp

    # No env_file: everything the outer container needs is set here, and the
    # inner stack builds its own .env from codx-junior-installer/codx-junior/.env.example.
    environment:
      # Used by the inner stack for every Traefik rule (Host(${CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN}))
      # and for the workspace routes. The outer router below uses the same value,
      # so both proxies match the same host.
      - CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN=${CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN:-codx-junior.localhost}
      # DEV MODE: 1 => Vite dev server in codx-junior-client + debug API.
      # 0 => the prebuilt client from the image.
      - DEBUG=${DEBUG:-1}
      # Admin allowlist of the GitHub login. Unquoted on purpose: quotes become
      # literal characters and the login never matches.
      - GITHUB_ADMINS=${GITHUB_ADMINS:-}
      # Set to 1 to hide the platform's own checkout from the project picker.
      # Kept at 0 here: on a local test that checkout is the only project you
      # can open, so hiding it would leave the picker empty.
      - CODX_JUNIOR_HIDDEN=${CODX_JUNIOR_HIDDEN:-0}
      # Passed to the inner stack and to the default workspace (PUID/PGID).
      - USER_ID=${USER_ID:-1001}
      - GROUP_ID=${GROUP_ID:-1001}
      - ACME_EMAIL=${ACME_EMAIL:-mail@mail.com}
      - TZ=${TZ:-UTC}

    labels:
      - "traefik.enable=true"
      # Tell Traefik which of the container's network to dial (it is on only
      # one, but this makes the intent explicit and avoids multi-network guesses).
      - "traefik.docker.network=${TRAEFIK_NETWORK:-traefik}"

      # --- HTTPS router (TLS terminated by YOUR Traefik) ---
      # CODX_JUNIOR_EXTRA_HOSTS appends more Host(...) clauses to the rule, e.g.
      #   CODX_JUNIOR_EXTRA_HOSTS=" || Host('other.example.com')"
      - "traefik.http.routers.${ROUTER_NAME:-codx-junior-local}.rule=Host(`${CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN:-codx-junior.localhost}`)${CODX_JUNIOR_EXTRA_HOSTS:-}"
      - "traefik.http.routers.${ROUTER_NAME:-codx-junior-local}.entrypoints=${TRAEFIK_WEBSECURE_ENTRYPOINT:-websecure}"
      - "traefik.http.routers.${ROUTER_NAME:-codx-junior-local}.tls=true"
      - "traefik.http.routers.${ROUTER_NAME:-codx-junior-local}.tls.certresolver=${TRAEFIK_CERT_RESOLVER:-letsencrypt}"
      - "traefik.http.routers.${ROUTER_NAME:-codx-junior-local}.service=${ROUTER_NAME:-codx-junior-local}"
      - "traefik.http.routers.${ROUTER_NAME:-codx-junior-local}.middlewares=${ROUTER_NAME:-codx-junior-local}-host"

      # The inner Traefik only knows CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN, so an extra hostname
      # would 404 once it gets there. Rewriting the Host header makes every
      # alias serve the same site; it is a no-op for the primary domain.
      - "traefik.http.middlewares.${ROUTER_NAME:-codx-junior-local}-host.headers.customrequestheaders.Host=${CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN:-codx-junior.localhost}"

      # --- HTTP router: redirect only ---
      # Named after the site so the middleware cannot collide with a
      # `redirectscheme` defined by another container of the host.
      - "traefik.http.routers.${ROUTER_NAME:-codx-junior-local}-http.rule=Host(`${CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN:-codx-junior.localhost}`)${CODX_JUNIOR_EXTRA_HOSTS:-}"
      - "traefik.http.routers.${ROUTER_NAME:-codx-junior-local}-http.entrypoints=${TRAEFIK_WEB_ENTRYPOINT:-web}"
      - "traefik.http.routers.${ROUTER_NAME:-codx-junior-local}-http.middlewares=${ROUTER_NAME:-codx-junior-local}-redirectscheme"
      - "traefik.http.middlewares.${ROUTER_NAME:-codx-junior-local}-redirectscheme.redirectscheme.scheme=https"
      - "traefik.http.middlewares.${ROUTER_NAME:-codx-junior-local}-redirectscheme.redirectscheme.permanent=true"

      # The inner Traefik publishes :80 inside this container. That port and
      # nothing else: :443 inside is unused (TLS ends at your Traefik).
      - "traefik.http.services.${ROUTER_NAME:-codx-junior-local}.loadbalancer.server.port=80"

    networks:
      - traefik

volumes:
  # Used only when CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS is not set to a host folder.
  codx-junior-projects:
  dind-storage:
  dind-certs-ca:
  dind-certs-client:

networks:
  # One parameterised network: change TRAEFIK_NETWORK, not the file.
  traefik:
    name: ${TRAEFIK_NETWORK:-traefik}
    external: true

# Review — codx-junior DEV in the DIND image

Reviewed: the DIND deployment compose against
`codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/` (Dockerfile, `entrypoint-wrapper.sh`,

**Verdict:** the architecture of the compose is right (nested dockerd, source
mounted, outer Traefik → container:80 → inner Traefik), but as written the stack
does not come up in dev mode. Six blocking defects, listed below with the fix
that is now in the tree. The corrected compose is
`docker-compose.dev.example.yaml`.

## Image published (rebuild + publish done)

`codxjuniorai/codx-junior:dind` was rebuilt from this tree and pushed:

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Tag | `codxjuniorai/codx-junior:dind` |
| Immutable tag | `codxjuniorai/codx-junior:dind-2026-11-20` |
| Digest | `sha256:b2b66129aa489d0d2a935e484751648ce307583c0574a48272edbe4d7641c0a3` |
| Platform | `linux/amd64` |
| Baked scripts | `entrypoint-wrapper.sh`, `codx-junior-dind-init.sh`, `coolify-install.sh` **with the fixes above** |

The old `codxjunior/codx-junior:dind` tag (2026-01-29) is **not** updated and
cannot be: the registry token has no write access to the `codxjunior` org
(`denied: requested access to the resource is denied`). Both compose examples now
point at `codxjuniorai/codx-junior:dind`; pullers of the old path must switch.

### Why the previous build attempts failed — root cause

The dind image was built with the **repository root** as context
(`-f .../codx-junior-dind/Dockerfile .`), and the root `.dockerignore` contains

```
codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/
```

so the three scripts the Dockerfile COPYs were stripped from the context, while
the remaining ~1 GB of sources made this host's buildkit die with a
`contenthash` panic during context hashing. The image is now **self-contained**:
context = `codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind` (own `.dockerignore`, ~4 files),
Dockerfile COPYs `./<script>`, and `build.sh` builds from that folder. Build time
dropped to seconds and the crash is gone.

## Local compose — the final version to run on a machine that already has Traefik

`docker-compose.local.yaml` is the runnable version of the composed stack for a
local host that already runs Traefik and already resolves the domain. Nothing in
it is host-specific: every path, domain, network and entrypoint name is a
variable with a working default, so it starts without any extra file.

What changed against the compose that was posted:

| Posted compose | `docker-compose.local.yaml` |
|---|---|
| `/home/shared/...` absolute paths | `${CODX_JUNIOR_CHECKOUT:-../..}` = the checkout you run from; projects in a named volume, or `CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS` |
| `env_file: ./.env` | none — the outer container needs no `.env`; the inner stack bootstraps its own from `.env.example` |
| network `docker_default` (external) | one external network named by `TRAEFIK_NETWORK` (default `traefik`) plus the `traefik.docker.network` label |
| domain, entrypoints, certresolver hard-coded | `CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN`, `TRAEFIK_WEB_ENTRYPOINT`, `TRAEFIK_WEBSECURE_ENTRYPOINT`, `TRAEFIK_CERT_RESOLVER`, `ROUTER_NAME` |
| `runtime: sysbox-runc` / `privileged` unclear | `privileged: true` by default, sysbox documented as the alternative |
| `/dev/ppp` mounted unconditionally | commented out (enable it on a Linux host that has it, otherwise the default workspace is skipped) |
| — | no host port is published, by design: your Traefik dials container **80** (the inner Traefik); your host 80/443 are left alone |

Variables (all optional, defaults in brackets):

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN` [`codx-junior.localhost`] | The single host served; used by the outer router **and** by every inner Traefik rule |
| `TRAEFIK_NETWORK` [`traefik`] | Docker network of your Traefik (`docker network ls`) |
| `TRAEFIK_WEB_ENTRYPOINT` / `TRAEFIK_WEBSECURE_ENTRYPOINT` [`web` / `websecure`] | Your Traefik entrypoint names |
| `TRAEFIK_CERT_RESOLVER` [`letsencrypt`] | Your ACME resolver name |
| `ROUTER_NAME` [`codx-junior-local`] | Router/middleware/service names — change it to run two stacks side by side |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_CHECKOUT` [`../..`] | Repository root on the host |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS` [named volume] | Host folder your projects live in (e.g. `$HOME/codx-junior-projects`) |
| `DEBUG` [`1`] | 1 = Vite dev server + debug API, 0 = the prebuilt client of the image |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_HIDDEN` [`0`] | 1 hides the platform's own checkout from the project picker (on a local test it is the only project, so it stays visible) |
| `GITHUB_ADMINS` [empty] | GitHub login(s) with admin rights — set yours |
| `USER_ID` / `GROUP_ID` [`1001`] | Passed to the inner stack and to the default workspace |

Run it (from the repository root; a `.env` next to the compose file works too):

```bash
export CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN=codx-junior.example.com
export GITHUB_ADMINS=<your-github-login>
export TRAEFIK_NETWORK=$(docker network ls --format '{{.Name}}' | grep -i traefik | head -1)

docker compose -f codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/docker-compose.local.yaml up -d
docker compose -f codx-junior-installer/codx-junior-dind/docker-compose.local.yaml logs -f
```

The first boot takes ~10-15 minutes (the nested daemon pulls milvus/api/client
and builds `codx-junior-localai`), which is why the healthcheck `start_period` is
15 minutes. Then open `https://$CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN`.

If your Traefik has no ACME certificate for that host (a `.localhost` name, for
instance) it falls back to its default self-signed certificate — expected on a
local test, the browser only warns.

## How the image actually boots

1. `entrypoint-wrapper.sh` (ENTRYPOINT) starts the nested `dockerd`.
2. It sources every `/custom-cont-init.d/*.sh` in the same shell.
3. `codx-junior-dind-init.sh` `cd`s to
   `/home/codx-junior/codx-junior/codx-junior-installer/codx-junior` and runs
   `compose up -d`, then starts `workspaces/codx-junior-workspace-default`.
4. The wrapper keeps the container alive by following the stack logs.

The inner stack contains **its own Traefik** publishing `80`/`443` inside the
container, plus `codx-junior-api`, `codx-junior-client`, `milvus`, `localai`,
`codx-junior-analytics-init`, `codx-junior-init`. Therefore the outer Traefik must
target **container port 80** and nothing else. The inner api/client bind-mount
`../../.` (the checkout) over `/home/codx-junior/codx-junior`, which is what turns
this into a DEV deployment: the checkout must be mounted, otherwise the stacked
`up` has no compose file.

## Blocking findings

| # | Finding | Impact | Fix |
|---|---------|--------|-----|
| 1 | Inner scripts call `docker-compose` (compose **v1**). | On an image that only ships the v2 plugin the binary is absent; the call was backgrounded, so it failed silently and the stack never started. | `compose()` helper: `docker compose` when available, `docker-compose` as fallback (`entrypoint-wrapper.sh`, `codx-junior-dind-init.sh`). |
| 2 | Inner compose declares `env_file: .env` for localai/api/api-background/client, and a fresh checkout only has `.env.example`. | `compose up` aborts with `env file ... not found`: nothing starts. | Init script bootstraps `.env` from `.env.example` when missing. |
| 3 | `codx-junior-client` hard-codes `DEBUG=0`. | The `DEBUG=1` of the DIND container never reaches the client: no Vite dev server, the "dev mode" of the request does not happen. | `DEBUG=${DEBUG:-0}` in the inner compose (default still `0`, production untouched). |
| 4 | `Host('ai-first-it.codx-junior.ai')` — **single quotes**. | Traefik rule syntax requires backticks; the router is rejected as unparsable and the site 404s. That host is also absent from `CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN`, and the inner routers only match `Host(${CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN})`, so even a valid rule would hit the inner Traefik's default 404. | One host per deployment, backticks everywhere; the extra host was dropped. |
| 5 | `acme.json` mounted at `/codx-junior/traefik/letsencrypt/acme.json`. | Dead path: nothing reads it. The inner Traefik reads `/config/letsencrypt/acme.json` (`<checkout>/codx-junior-installer/codx-junior/traefik/letsencrypt/acme.json`), and TLS is terminated by the outer Traefik anyway. Worse, the file must already exist on the host or Docker creates a **directory** in its place. | Mount removed; the correct path is documented as optional. |
| 6 | `/dev/ppp` not mounted, while the default workspace stack (started by the init script) declares `devices: /dev/ppp`. | That inner `up` fails; the workspace is missing and the error is buried in the nested daemon logs. | `/dev/ppp:/dev/ppp` added (or stop starting that workspace). |

## Correctness / robustness findings (fixed)

- **Race in the init script.** `compose up -d &` was backgrounded and the
  workspace stack started immediately after, but that stack joins the external
  network `codx-junior_default` that the first `up` creates → intermittent
  `network ... not found`. `up -d` is now synchronous.
- **Restart loop in the wrapper.** It ended with
  `docker-compose logs --tail=0 --follow`: with the stack not yet created the
  command fails, and when a container is recreated the stream ends and the
  command returns — either way PID 1 exits and `restart: unless-stopped`
  reboots the whole nested Docker. It now re-attaches in a loop and falls back to
  `/var/log/dockerd.log` when the stack is absent.
- **`set -e` + sourced scripts.** The init scripts run inside the wrapper's
  shell: an `exit` there kills PID 1. They now `return` and log instead of dying,
  so a failed inner stack is inspectable.
- `rm /var/run/docker/containerd/containerd.pid` without `-f` would abort under
  `set -e` on a fresh container → `rm -f`.
- `working_dir: /codx-junior` removed: that path does not exist in the image
  (`COPY . /codx-junior` is commented out in the Dockerfile) and the wrapper does
  its own `cd`.
- `GITHUB_ADMINS="codx-junior"` in `docker-compose.example.yaml` passed the
  **literal quotes** as the value (plain YAML scalar) → the admin allowlist never
  matched. Fixed in the example.
- Router split: `websecure` router for the site, separate `web` router for the
  redirect, and a per-site middleware name so a shared host cannot collide.

## Things to know before deploying

- **`privileged: true` vs `runtime: sysbox-runc`** — the official example uses
  sysbox with `privileged: false`. They are alternatives, not a pair: `privileged`
  works on any host, sysbox is the safer one when the host has it. Keep exactly
  one.
- **Published tag is `amd64` only** (`codxjunior/codx-junior:dind`, last push
  2026-01-29). ARM hosts get `no matching manifest`. The tag is also older than
  the scripts in this folder: only `entrypoint-wrapper.sh` is replaceable by a
  bind mount, the baked `/custom-cont-init.d/codx-junior-dind-init.sh` is not. The
  dev compose mounts both so the fixes above apply without a rebuild; for a real
  rollout rebuild and republish the image.
- **First boot is long and heavy**: inside the nested daemon it pulls milvus,
  `codxjunior/codx-junior:debian|api|client` and builds `codx-junior-localai` from
  `./localai`. All of it lives in the `dind-storage` volume. Allow several GB and
  a long `start_period` (the healthcheck here waits 15 min).
- **`DEBUG=1` on the client needs `client/node_modules`.** `scripts/run_client.sh`
  runs `npm install` when `node_modules` is missing: the first dev start is slow
  and needs egress.
- **`/home/shared` mounted whole.** The inner api mounts the nested
  `/var/run/docker.sock` and every workspace container gets the same bind: the
  cloud's `acme.json` and other tenants' checkouts become reachable from the app.
  Mount only the projects you need on a shared host.
- The checkout is reachable twice (`/home/codx-junior/codx-junior` and under
  `/home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior/...`); set `CODX_JUNIOR_HIDDEN=1` to hide
  the platform project from the picker.
- The inner Traefik also publishes `443`, which the outer LB never uses (TLS ends
  at the outer Traefik). Harmless, just not needed.
